subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
Checking the side view render, I notice the gold plate positioned right under the runes is actually overlapping and hiding the rune plane entirely since their spans overlap — that's a bug to fix.

I'll move the rune plane further out past the gold plate so it's visible, and rethink the plate's color — maybe a dark navy backing instead of flat gold so the glowing runes stand out better. I also spot the same overlap issue in the three-quarter view on the opposite side, needing the same correction.

Looking at the back view now, it reads as nearly pure black since there's no texture and no direct lighting hits it — I'm considering adding a decorative plane there, maybe reusing the sky texture, to break up the void.

For the back panel specifically, I want to swap the dark wood tone for a lighter grain treatment and add an emblem, since the current dark color combined with cel-shading makes it look flat and lifeless.

I also realize the crescent finial on top is extruding in the wrong plane — it's rotated so it appears edge-on from the front instead of facing the viewer, so I need to fix the extrusion axis so the crescent actually opens outward as intended.

I'm double-checking shelf placements and confirming the top shelf matches the skull/books/orb arrangement in the render, then noting minor stray elements like shadows and floating orbs can be left as-is. I'm also reviewing the back panel box's position and dimensions relative to the sky plane to make sure it stays hidden behind the front view correctly.

Now I'm deciding to just recolor the back panel with a lighter wood grain tone rather than adding a separate plane, since the box's back face only picks up ambient lighting anyway — swapping to a warmer grain color like "#8a5a38" should look fine without affecting other visible surfaces.

Switching to refining the side rune plate: adjusting positions for the navy plate and gold runes slightly outward, and adding a thin gold frame behind the navy plate for a bordered look.
